tagline: Leading manufacturer of water heating and treatment solutions
hero_kpi_rationale: The North America segment represents 78% of total sales and is the primary driver of growth and profitability, supported by key regulatory dynamics (DOE energy efficiency standards) and significant price increases offsetting cost pressures.
company_description: A. O. Smith Corporation manufactures and markets residential and commercial gas and electric water heaters, boilers, heat pumps, tanks, and water treatment products in North America, China, Europe, and India. The company offers water heaters for residences, restaurants, hotels, office buildings, laundries, car washes, and small businesses; boilers for hospitals, schools, hotels, homes, apartments, and condominiums, and other large commercial buildings; and water treatment products comprising point-of-entry water softeners, well water solutions, and whole-home water filtration products, and point-of-use carbon and reverse osmosis products for residences, restaurants, hotels, and offices. It also provides commercial water treatment and filtration products; expansion tanks, commercial solar water heating systems, swimming pool and spa heaters, and related products and parts; and electric wall-hung, gas tankless, combi-boiler, and heat pump and solar water heaters. The company offers its products under the A. O. Smith, State, Lochinvar, Hague, Water-Right, Master Water, Atlantic Filter, Impact, and Water Tec brands. kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Portion of profit after cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: Gross margin improves from 38.1% in 2024 to 38.8% in 2025, driven by price increases and a better contribution from commercial products.
kpis.signal: Improvement due to pricing and a more profitable product mix.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.description: Calculated as pre-tax income (715.1M) / sales (3,830.2M), operating margin is stable at approximately 18.7% in 2025 versus 18.4% in 2024.
kpis.signal: Slight improvement despite higher overhead expenses.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total annual sales of the company.
kpis.description: Revenue increases from $3,818.1M in 2024 to $3,830.2M in 2025, a 0.3% rise, driven by price increases, commercial volumes, and the Pureit acquisition.
kpis.signal: Very modest growth, driven by pricing and acquisitions.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending on new equipment or production capacity.
kpis.description: The company maintains capital expenditures at approximately $120M to support commercial capacity and comply with DOE energy efficiency regulations for commercial water heaters effective October 2026.
kpis.signal: Stable Capex to support DOE regulatory compliance.

kpis.name: North America Sales
kpis.explanation: Sales generated in the North America region.
kpis.description: North America sales represent 78% of total sales, increasing 1.2% in 2025 ($2,984.2M vs $2,950.1M in 2024), driven by commercial boilers and water heaters.
kpis.signal: Growth supported by commercial products and price increases.

kpis.name: China Sales (third-party)
kpis.explanation: Sales generated in China to external customers (excluding intercompany sales).
kpis.description: China sales decline by 12% in local currency in 2025, impacted by weak consumer demand and the discontinuation of government subsidy programs in the second half of the year.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline in China in local currency due to weak demand and subsidy removal.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €3.14 Bn in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €0.19 Bn in the latest year

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $0.72 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $0.196 Bn in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout ratio = Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the last four fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Portion of net income distributed as dividends: 35.8% in the latest year.

kpis.name: Pureit Contribution
kpis.explanation: Sales generated from the Pureit acquisition since November 2024.
kpis.description: The acquisition of Pureit in November 2024 from Unilever for $125M contributed $54M in sales in 2025 within the Rest of World segment, doubling market penetration in South Asia with a broad range of residential water purification solutions.
kpis.signal: Strategic acquisition doubling South Asia market penetration.

kpis.name: Commercial Water Heater Growth
kpis.explanation: Growth in sales of water heaters for commercial applications.
kpis.description: Commercial water heater volumes increased by approximately 5% in 2025, ahead of the new DOE energy efficiency regulations effective October 2026. Growth is estimated at 3% to 5% in 2026 due to a pull-forward effect as products subject to regulatory phase-out are purchased early.
kpis.signal: Growth due to pull-forward demand ahead of DOE regulation.

risks.title: Global economic downturn and demand weakness
risks.summary: A global recession or economic slowdown would reduce consumer confidence and demand for water heaters and water treatment products, negatively impacting margins and cash flows.
risks.score_rationale: Risk ranked first in the section (strong position), intense language 'could materially adversely affect', stable trend but deteriorating macro backdrop (recession, inflation), macro category heavily weighted for cyclical sector.

risks.title: Tariffs and trade restrictions
risks.summary: New U.S. tariffs would increase costs of essential raw materials, forcing AOS to raise prices or compress margins, with risk of trade retaliation.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk in economic section, highly intense language 'could significantly increase the prices' and 'could have a material adverse effect', increasing trend (new administration, announced tariffs), direct impact on critical raw material costs.

risks.title: Customer concentration and commercial dependency
risks.summary: The top five customers represent 41% of sales. Loss of a major customer, order reductions, or customer financial instability would directly threaten financial results.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly identified risk with key figure (41% of sales from 5 customers), language 'could have a material adverse effect', stable but structural trend, high credit weighting due to customer dependency.

risks.title: Geographic exposure to China and uncertainty
risks.summary: China represents 18% of sales and 4,200 employees. The announced strategic review creates uncertainty among customers and suppliers, while weak Chinese economic conditions reduce demand.
risks.score_rationale: Specific risk with quantified data (18% of sales, 4,200 employees, $140M in cash), language 'could materially and adversely affect', increasing trend (12% decline in 2025, strategic review announced), high geopolitical weighting.

risks.title: Raw material price volatility and supplier concentration
risks.summary: Steel and component prices are volatile. AOS relies on a limited number of suppliers for certain critical raw materials, with a historical lag in passing cost increases to customers.
risks.score_rationale: Major operational risk with concrete examples (steel, freight inflation), language 'could lead to lower operating earnings' and 'material adverse effect', increasing trend (recent inflation, potential tariffs), high industrial weighting.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and sensitive data protection
risks.summary: AOS collects sensitive data (customers, employees, intellectual property). Cybersecurity incidents could disrupt operations and damage reputation, with heightened risks from remote work and AI.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly identified risk with operational details (customer data, employee data, third-party systems), language 'could adversely affect our business and reputation', stable trend but rising risks (AI, remote work), cybersecurity heavily weighted.

risks.title: Technological change and shifting consumer preferences
risks.summary: Consumers are shifting toward electric and decarbonized products. AOS must adapt its product portfolio and distribution channels (e-commerce) to remain competitive amid rapid changes.
risks.score_rationale: Major strategic risk with explicit trends (decarbonization, electrification, e-commerce), language 'could materially and adversely affect', increasing trend (ongoing energy transition), high technology weighting.

risks.title: Extraordinary events and natural disasters
risks.summary: Two AOS plants are located in flood-prone areas that have experienced flooding. Natural disasters, wars, or health crises could disrupt production and reduce consumer demand.
risks.score_rationale: Operational risk with concrete exposure (2 plants in flood zones, seismic/hurricane areas), language 'could significantly disrupt production' and 'materially and adversely affect', stable trend but worsened by climate change, moderate environmental weighting.

ai_positioning.summary: The company AOS has no significant mentions regarding artificial intelligence, machine learning, or similar technologies in the provided excerpts from the 10-K/20-F filing.
